# tarsi.toml schema

The config document is `tarsi_core::Config` — TOML or YAML
(`tarsi.yaml`/`tarsi.yml` preferred on discovery ties). Pure serde
types in `crates/tarsi-core/src/config.rs`; loading/layering in
`tarsi-config`. Secret **names** appear (`token_env`); values never
do.
<!-- generated by cypera gen config — field tables come from the
     config structs; prose sections are curated in cypera.toml -->

## Top level

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | `string` | optional | Named release profile to layer *under* this config — a `type: tarsi` tamias pack or a dir under `~/.config/tarsi/profiles/`. Resolved by `tarsi-config` (profile dir becomes a config layer between the repo file and the user file); ignored by planning itself. |
| `release` | `ReleaseConfig` | optional | — |
| `publish` | `PublishConfig` | optional | — |

## `[release]`

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `units` | `UnitsSpec` | optional | How release units resolve. Default: cargo workspace at root. |
| `tag_format` | `string` | optional | Default tag template for units that don't override it. |
| `changelog_path` | `string` | optional | Changelog file spliced per unit — resolved relative to each unit's path (`crates/foo` + `CHANGES.md` → `crates/foo/CHANGES.md`). |
| `styleguide` | `string` | optional | keep-a-changelog \| conventional-commit-grouped \| …  **Deprecated (P-030)** — superseded by [`ReleaseConfig::strategy`]'s `changelog` section table. Still parsed for backward compat; has no effect on planning (it never did — the field was always descriptive). |
| `strategy` | `StrategyRef` | optional | Release strategy (P-030): a builtin name (`"conventional"`, `"semantic-release-angular"`) or an inline rules table (`[release.strategy.bump]` / `[release.strategy.changelog]`). Absent = `conventional`, the pre-strategy behavior. Resolved inside `tarsi-serve`'s plan path so every op inherits it. |
| `default_bump` | `Bump` | optional | Repo-wide default bump when inference finds nothing — honored as the strategy's `fallback` (P-030 wired the previously-dead field; an explicit `strategy.bump.fallback` wins). |
| `diff_exclude` | `list` | optional | Path globs excluded from commit→unit attribution (e.g. `["docs/**", "*.md"]`). Wired in P-030: matching paths are stripped from each commit before attribution; a commit left with no paths is dropped entirely. |
| `unit_overrides` | `BTreeMap<String, UnitOverride>` | optional | Per-unit overrides keyed by unit name. |
| `sync_refs` | `SyncRefsConfig` | optional | Pack-ref/doc version sync — rewrite stale `name@old` / manifest `version:` refs in repo files *before* the release commit lands, so the tagged tree is self-consistent (T-039; replaces the per-repo `scripts/release.sh` pre-step). Empty `rules` = disabled — repos opt in. |

### `[release] strategy`

The release *policy* as data (P-030): bump inference and changelog
sectioning. Either a builtin name or an inline table — absent means
`conventional`, the pre-strategy behavior.

```toml
strategy = "conventional"            # builtin name, OR inline:

[release.strategy.bump]
fallback = "patch"                   # bump when no rule matches

[[release.strategy.bump.rules]]
type = "feat"                        # raw conventional type token; "*"/absent = any
scope = "core-*"                     # optional: exact or trailing-* glob
breaking = true                      # optional: pin the !/BREAKING CHANGE flag
not_type = ["fix"]                   # optional: type tokens that veto the match
bump = "minor"                       # major|minor|patch|none

[release.strategy.changelog]
[[release.strategy.changelog.sections]]
key = "added"                        # stable section id
heading = "Added"                    # rendered as `### Added`
[[release.strategy.changelog.sections.rules]]
type = "feat"                        # same matcher fields, no `bump`
```

Semantics:

- **Bump rules are max-match** — a commit contributes the highest
  `bump` across its matching rules; a unit folds max across its
  commits (semantic-release commit-analyzer's "highest release
  type wins" — rule order can't be gamed). `fallback` applies when
  inference finds nothing; `release.default_bump` fills it when the
  strategy doesn't set one.
- **Changelog sections are first-match** — a commit lands in the
  first section (table order) with a matching rule; table order is
  also render order. Commits matching nothing are dropped.
- Matchers run on the commit's **raw type token** — `deps`,
  `i18n`, and other non-`CommitKind` types are nameable.
- Each absent `strategy.*` sub-table defaults to the `conventional`
  rules, so `[release.strategy.bump]` alone keeps the conventional
  changelog.
- Builtin names: `conventional` (default — byte-identical to the
  pre-P-030 hardcoded policy), `semantic-release-angular` (the
  commit-analyzer angular preset as data), and `keep-a-changelog`
  (the keepachangelog.com section layout — see below).
- The resolved strategy echoes on `plan` results as
  `plan.strategy {name, resolved}` (`name` = the builtin name or
  `"custom"`).

What can't be data stays code: changelog render formats beyond
section/heading/order, non-semver versioning, non-conventional
commit parsing, anything needing execution (P-030 boundary).

#### `keep-a-changelog`

Keep a Changelog (keepachangelog.com) is a *changelog layout*, not
a bump policy — the builtin keeps `conventional`'s bump rules
verbatim and swaps only the section table for the six canonical
sections, in keepachangelog.com order:

| section | commits |
| --- | --- |
| `### Added` | `feat` |
| `### Changed` | `refactor`, plus breaking commits of types with no section of their own (`chore!`, `deps!`, unknown `!` types) |
| `### Deprecated` | `deprecate`, `deprecation` |
| `### Removed` | `revert`, `remove` |
| `### Fixed` | `fix`, `perf` |
| `### Security` | `security` |

Breaking commits of section-owning types stay in their own
section (`fix!`→Fixed, `security!`→Security, …) — Changed's
catch-all vetoes them via `not_type`. Types outside the table
(`chore`, `docs`, `test`, `deps`, `release`, …) still count for
bump inference but are dropped from the changelog. KaC-named
types (`deprecate`, `revert`, `remove`, `security`) are
changelog-only here — they don't move the version unless
`default_bump` fills the fallback; a repo that wants e.g.
`revert`→patch takes the same table inline with one extra bump
rule.

### `[release.unit_overrides.<name>]`

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bump` | `Bump` | optional | Force this unit's bump (beats inference). |
| `tag_format` | `string` | optional | Per-unit tag template. |
| `publish` | `Vec<PublishTarget>` | optional | Restrict publish targets (`"crates-io"`, `"github-release"`). |
| `skip` | `bool` | optional | Skip this unit entirely (e.g. a lib that versions with its parent). |

### `[release.sync_refs]`

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rules` | `Vec<SyncRefRule>` | optional | Rewrite rules, applied in order. Empty = the stage is disabled entirely (no files touched, no step reported). |

#### sync rule (`rules[]` entries)

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `files` | `list` | optional | Repo-root-relative globs of files to rewrite (`"libraries/myco/tamias.yaml"`, `"README.md"`, `".agents/skills/myco/SKILL.md"`). Non-matching globs are skipped — a repo can carry rules for files it doesn't have. |
| `find` | `string` | required | Regex matching the stale ref. Required. |
| `replace` | `string` | required | Literal replacement text. Required — an empty string would silently delete refs, so serde rejects a missing key. |

Rewrites stale version refs in repo files *inside* the `bump`/`release`
pipeline — after manifests are bumped, before the release commit — so
the tagged tree is self-consistent. This is the stage that replaced the
per-repo `scripts/release.sh` plan+`sed` pre-step (T-039): pack
`tamias.yaml` manifest versions and `name@ver` README/SKILL install
examples.

```toml
[release.sync_refs]
rules = [
  # pack manifest version line (line anchor needs (?m))
  { files = ["libraries/myco/tamias.yaml"],
    find = "(?m)^version: \"{old}\"",
    replace = "version: \"{new}\"" },
  # doc refs — global, like the old `sed s|name@old|name@new|g`
  { files = ["README.md", ".agents/skills/myco/SKILL.md"],
    find = "myco@{old}",
    replace = "myco@{new}" },
]
```

`{old}`/`{new}` expand to the releasing units' shared
`current_version`/`new_version`. Inside `find` they are
regex-escaped (so `.` stays literal); inside `replace` they expand
literally. Patterns are **not** auto-bounded — `app@{old}` matches
the `app@1.2.3` prefix of `app@1.2.30`, exactly like the old `sed`
pre-steps; add `\b` when a boundary is needed (`regex` has no
look-around). Use `(?m)` for line anchors.

Semantics:

- **Single-version only** — sync needs one unambiguous `old → new`
  pair. A plan whose releasing units disagree on `new_version` (or
  `current_version`) reports `status:"skipped"` and the release
  proceeds unsynced — the shims' `len(vs)==1` guard.
- **Idempotent** — rules match the *old* version; once refs say
  `new`, nothing matches and the stage reports zero changes.
- **Dry-run** — `bump`/`release` with `dry_run:true` (the default)
  reports `status:"dry-run"` plus `changed_files` without writing.
- Results surface as `sync_refs{status, reason?, old, new,
  changes[], changed_files?}` on `bump` and `release`; `steps_run`
  gains a `"sync-refs"` entry between `bump-manifests` and
  `commit-bump` when rules are configured. Synced files are staged
  into the release commit itself — no separate pre-commit.

## `[publish]`

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `crates` | `CratesPublish` | optional | crates.io publish target. |
| `ghreleases` | `GhReleasePublish` | optional | GitHub Releases publish target. |
| `dry_run` | `bool` | optional | Schema-level dry-run flag; the serve op's `dry_run` param is what callers use. |

### `[publish.crates]`

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | optional | crates.io publishing on/off. |
| `retry_429` | `bool` | optional | Retry crates.io 429s with backoff (release.sh semantics). |
| `max_attempts` | `int` | optional | Max publish attempts per unit. |
| `token_env` | `string` | optional | Env var NAME consulted for the crates.io token when `token_ref` is unset or misses — cargo reads `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, and a resolved value is injected into the publish child's environment under that name. The value never appears in config, manifests, or logs. |
| `token_ref` | `string` | optional | Optional `cuora://&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;name&gt;` secret ref — resolved via cuora at publish time and takes precedence over `token_env`. The value never appears in config or logs. |

### `[publish.ghreleases]`

| key | type | required | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `bool` | optional | GitHub Releases on/off. |
| `token_env` | `string` | optional | Env var NAME holding the GitHub token — resolved via environment/cuora at publish time; the value never appears in config, manifests, or logs. |
| `repo` | `string` | optional | Repo override `owner/name`; default = git remote. |
| `token_ref` | `string` | optional | Optional `cuora://&lt;scope&gt;/&lt;name&gt;` secret ref — resolved via cuora at publish time and takes precedence over `token_env`. The value never appears in config or logs. |
| `assets` | `list` | optional | Repo-root-relative glob patterns for release assets — `{unit}` and `{version}` expand per releasing unit, e.g. `["dist/{unit}-{version}-*", "{unit}/checksums.txt"]`. A pattern with no glob magic must match an existing file; magic patterns matching nothing are skipped. Empty = notes-only releases. |

`bump` values: `"major"` | `"minor"` | `"patch"` | `"none"`.
`PublishTarget` values: `"crates-io"` | `"github-release"`.

## Layering

With a profile resolved, config loads through
`LayeredFileSource` — objects merge key-wise, later layers fill gaps:

```
repo tarsi.*  >  profile tarsi.*  >  ~/.config/tarsi/  >  defaults
```

Without a profile, discovery is first-match:
`$TARSI_CONFIG` → `./tarsi.*` → `~/.config/tarsi/`. A missing
profile name is a hard error; a present-but-broken `tarsi.*` file
always errors loudly.

## Example

See `tarsi.toml` at the repo root (dogfooding config) and
`libraries/9aia-release/tarsi.toml` (the org profile).

## Constraints

- Secret **names** (`token_env`, `token_ref`) appear in config;
  values never do — `cuora://` refs resolve via cuora at publish
  time, env names resolve through the environment.
- Unknown fields are not rejected at this layer — `deny_unknown_fields`
  is not set on the config structs; typos surface as ignored keys,
  so check `tarsi-serve` plan output when a key seems inert.
